questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Direct coalescence of particles moving in the same direction

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Direct coalescence of particles moving in the same direction

hints: When particles coalesce, their masses combine into $(m_A + m_B)$ and they share a single common velocity $v$.

walkthrough.text:
State the principle of conservation of linear momentum for two coalescing particles:
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = (m_A + m_B)v$$
Substitute $m_A = 0.4\text{ kg}$, $u_A = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $m_B = 0.6\text{ kg}$, and $u_B = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Evaluate the momentum terms and solve for $v$:
$$0.4(6) + 0.6(2) = (0.4 + 0.6)v$$
$$2.4 + 1.2 = 1.0v \implies v = 3.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the physical setup:
- Particle $A$: $m_A = 0.4\text{ kg}$, $u_A = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$
- Particle $B$: $m_B = 0.6\text{ kg}$, $u_B = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$
- Combined mass:
$$m_{\text{total}} = 0.4 + 0.6 = 1.0\text{ kg}$$

Equate total initial momentum to total final momentum:
$$p_{\text{initial}} = 0.4(6) + 0.6(2) = 2.4 + 1.2 = 3.6\text{ N s}$$
$$p_{\text{final}} = (1.0)v$$
$$1.0v = 3.6 \implies v = 3.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies conservation of linear momentum for coalescence: $m_A u_A + m_B u_B = (m_A + m_B)v$.

$$KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(0.5 + 0.5)(2^2) = \frac{1}{2}(1.0)(4) = 2.0\text{ J}$$

- Post-impact speed:
$$v = \frac{2.0}{1.0} = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

- Initial kinetic energy:
$$KE_i = \frac{1}{2}(0.5)(4^2) = 4\text{ J}$$
- Final kinetic energy:
$$KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(1.0)(2^2) = 2\text{ J}$$
